meta.purpose: Frozen contract: the exact page-global surface the _verify_* suite reaches into. A test bridge for the ES-module build must re-expose every symbol below whose kind is not "dom-id".
meta.method: acorn AST parse + scope walker (exact); no regex identifier scanning
caveats: refCount counts identifier occurrences across all page-side callbacks; fileCount counts distinct test files.
"written" means the symbol is the target of an assignment or ++/-- inside a page-side callback -> the bridge needs a SETTER, not just a getter.
"patched" means a property was assigned through the symbol (e.g. gl.bindBuffer=, TYPES.blur.eval=) -> the bridge must expose the LIVE object, never a copy.
Identifiers declared at index.html top level always win over the builtin deny-list, so app globals that shadow a DOM name (e.g. GPU) are never lost.
Page-side callbacks passed by NAME (page.evaluate(installHarness, arg)) are resolved to their Node-side declaration and analysed like inline ones.
meta.tests.unresolvedCallSites lists page-side calls with no analysable function argument (string bodies, handles). It must stay empty, or the surface is incomplete.
meta.tests.windowPropertyAccess lists every window.X touched from a page-side callback, flagged with whether X is an index.html global.

The surface is the UNION of the top-level declarations of every source in the app graph: each <script> in the HTML, each src= followed to disk, and each static (or literal dynamic) import followed transitively. Exported and non-exported top-level bindings both count; bare specifiers (npm packages) are never followed, so their bindings are not app surface.

symbols[].declModule / declLine say WHERE a declaration lives. --check deliberately ignores both: a declaration moving from index.html to src/legacy.js to src/core/gpu.js is the migration working, not the surface drifting. Only name/kind/written/patched are contract.

unbridgeable lists symbols an oracle touches that the appended accessor block cannot serve: declared outside meta.app.entryModule AND either not exported (so the entry module cannot name it) or WRITTEN (an imported binding cannot be assigned -- TypeError: Assignment to constant variable). Exported and read-only is fine. It must stay empty or the bridge cannot be generated as designed.

meta.app.moduleGoalFailures lists sources the HTML declares as modules that do not PARSE as modules (e.g. a duplicate top-level function declaration, legal in a classic script and a SyntaxError in a module). The browser would refuse such a file outright, so it is a hard failure here.
